headline: On last trading day, Sensex and Nifty plunged amid heavy FII selling and global risks

marketStatus.message: Market is closed for trading today due to an NSE holiday. It will reopen on Tuesday, 6 October.

why: En-masse selling by foreign institutional investors (FIIs) in the Indian market
Concerns over global rate hikes and cooling job markets in the US
Rising oil prices and global economic risks impacting investor sentiment
Indian benchmark shares posting their longest weekly losing run in 25 years
whatHappening: Sensex and Nifty extended their losing streak to an 8th consecutive week on Thursday
Approximately Rs 9 lakh crore of investor wealth was wiped out in a single session crash
PNB reported a 14.8% surge in advances with global business crossing Rs 31 lakh crore
The NSE and BSE are closed today, October 2, in observance of Gandhi Jayanti
summary: The Indian stock market is closed today for Gandhi Jayanti following a brutal Thursday session where the Sensex crashed significantly. Benchmarks recorded their eighth straight weekly decline, the longest losing streak in 25 years, driven by aggressive FII selling. While PNB reported strong Q2 business updates, broader sentiment remains dampened by global rate hike fears and oil price volatility.
